title: Specifier with `===` and no version is accepted instead of rejected
spec:
This is the `packaging` library (Python 3, no dependencies; the code is in `src/packaging/`). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests --ignore=tests/property` (about a minute).

The arbitrary-equality operator `===` is accepted with nothing after it, though it needs a version string.

```python
from packaging.specifiers import Specifier, SpecifierSet
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
Specifier("===")
Specifier("=== ")
SpecifierSet(">=1,===")
Requirement("foo===")
```

Expected: each raises `InvalidSpecifier` (`Requirement` raises `InvalidRequirement`).
Actual: each succeeds, e.g. `Specifier('===')` and `Requirement('foo===')`.

An empty (or whitespace-only) version after `===` must be invalid everywhere specifiers are parsed. `Specifier("===1.0")` and non-PEP 440 strings like `===foobar` must keep working.
acceptance: SpecifierSet containing a bare `===` raises InvalidSpecifier
